# Adjudication Task — Chapter 669

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃669화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|일다경(一茶頃). 아니, 어쩌면 촌각(寸刻).
  6|
  7|뇌옥의 모든 상황이 정리되기까지는 차 한잔 마실 시간도 걸리지 않았다.
  8|
  9|허기짐으로 반쯤 광폭화가 진행된 태산이 계단을 막고, 나를 선두로 야율목과 칠묘호가 나아가자 백족 전사들은 전의를 상실했다.
 10|
 11|나로서는 매우 다행스러운 일이었다.
 12|
 13|최대한 신속하게 뇌옥을 빠져나가야 하는 사정도 있었지만, 아직 중단전(中丹田)의 효용을 완전히 깨닫지 못한 나로서도 슬슬 한계를 느끼고 있었기 때문이다.
 14|
 15|이미 구속구를 끊는 데에 엄청난 심력(心力)을 소모한 와중에 한 차례의 짧은 전투까지, 속이 울렁거리고 가슴이 아파 오던 차에 등장한 태산은 천군만마나 다름없었다.
 16|
 17|“우워어어어!”
 18|
 19|음. 사실 저 정도면 헐크에 가깝나.
 20|
 21|그리고 적들의 빠른 투항에는 초절정 고수인 내 존재뿐만 아니라, 음산하기 짝이 없는 태산의 중얼거림이 크게 한몫했다.
 22|
 23|“%#$%&^&%^&%^#$!”
 24|
 25|“허억!”
 26|
 27|굶주림으로 번들거리는 눈동자.
 28|
 29|백족 전사들로서는 알아들을 수 없는 언어를 속사포처럼 내뱉으며 다가오는 태산의 모습이 공포, 그 자체였겠지만 나는 저 주문의 실체를 잘 알고 있었다.
 30|
 31|“오리구이 매채구육 어향육사 경장육사 산니백육 회과육 고노육 장우육 동파육 마파두부!”
 32|
 33|“…….”
 34|
 35|“궁보계정 향고유채 왕만두 규화계 탕초리적! 으아아아아!”
 36|
 37|음.
 38|
 39|놈들이 한어(漢語)를 알아듣지 못해서 참 다행이다. 어쩌면 신들린 듯이 음식 이름을 외치면서 천천히 다가오는 게 더 무서울 수도 있겠지만.
 40|
 41|“배애고오파아아아아아!”
 42|
 43|“히이이익! 사술이다! 저 괴물이 사술을 쓰려 한다!”
 44|
 45|“항복! 항복하겠소!”
 46|
 47|저 새끼 최소 남만 한정 사이어인.
 48|
 49|반응만 보면 배고파가 아니라 에네르기파인 줄 알겠다.
 50|
 51|물론 그런 내 생각과는 별개로 배고파의 효과는 확실했고, 이에 굴하지 않고 앞으로 나선 몇몇 용기 있는 놈들마저 태산에게 박살 나면서 상황은 끝났다.
 52|
 53|“두려워 말라! 돌겨역!”
 54|
 55|“할 수 있다! 놈을 쳐라!”
 56|
 57|앞으로 나선 놈들은 중원에서도 그럭저럭 초일류 취급받을 만큼 괜찮은 실력자들이었다.
 58|
 59|그들이 가진 유일한 문제는 상대가 영 좋지 않았다는 것뿐이다.
 60|
 61|퍽! 콰지직!
 62|
 63|우두둑!
 64|
 65|통나무처럼 굵은 팔다리가 휘둘려지자 사방으로 튕겨 나가는 신형들.
 66|
 67|그 모습을 확인한 백족 전사들은 침을 꿀꺽 삼키며 병장기를 내려놓았고, 야율목과 칠묘호는 아연한 눈빛으로 나를 바라봤다.
 68|
 69|“왜. 뭐.”
 70|
 71|“아니, 그. 공력 금제 당한 거 아니었나?”
 72|
 73|“아. 금제 당했지. 지금도 못 써.”
 74|
 75|“……그런데 어떻게.”
 76|
 77|“나는 말하자면 길고, 저놈은 그냥 타고났고.”
 78|
 79|인간의 신체는 기본적으로 한계가 있는 법인데, 시스템으로 그 한계를 아득히 뛰어넘은 나와 달리 태산은 자연적으로 발생한 괴물이다.
 80|
 81|공력이 없는 상태에서도 일류 고수 정도는 쥐잡듯 때려잡을 수 있을 정도로.
 82|
 83|‘어릴 때 감마선에 노출되기라도 했나.’
 84|
 85|나름 합리적인 의심이었지만, 지금 상황에서는 그게 중요한 게 아니다.
 86|
 87|나는 이미 전의를 상실한 채 스스로 무장을 해제한 백족 전사들을 바라보며 작게 중얼거렸다.
 88|
 89|“자. 우선 여기부터 정리하자고.”
 90|
 91|
 92|
 93|* * *
 94|
 95|
 96|
 97|결론부터 말하자면, 투항한 백족 전사들은 살아남았다. 정확히는 야율목이 그들을 살렸다.
 98|
 99|투둑. 털썩.
100|
101|점혈(點穴) 당한 몸뚱어리가 의식을 잃고 쓰러진다.
102|
103|며칠 전 애뇌산으로 향하는 길에 면식을 익힌 칠묘호가 그들을 한곳에 모아 뇌옥에 처박았고, 우리는 지체하지 않고 지상으로 이어진 계단으로 향했다.
104|
105|철벅.
106|
107|“아까도 말했지만…… 후회할 거야.”
108|
109|걸음과 함께 불쑥 던진 한마디. 그 말에 담긴 의미를 알아들은 야율목이 고개를 저었다.
110|
111|“그럴 일 없다.”
112|
113|“이미 얼굴도 훤히 드러난 마당에, 놈들이 정신을 차리게 되면 누구 이름부터 댈까.”
114|
115|야율목은 남만야수궁의 소궁주니 더 말할 것도 없고, 칠묘호 역시 묘족을 대표하는 전사들인 만큼 얼굴이 제법 알려진 자들.
116|
117|부족이 다르다고는 하지만 저들 중 일부는 이미 이들의 정체를 알아차렸을 것이다.
118|
119|“이 사실이 밝혀지는 건 시간문제야. 입을 막았어야 했어.”
120|
121|“상관없다.”
122|
123|“상관이 없긴, 염병하고 있네. 이 길로 도주할 것도 아니라면서 상관이 왜 없어? 만약 여기 남아 있으면…….”
124|
125|“정체가 밝혀지겠지. 당장 목숨이 위태롭지는 않겠지만 대회의의 결정을 거스른 대가를 톡톡히 치를 테고.”
126|
127|“이런 말 해서 미안하긴 한데, 혹시 좆 되는 취미 있냐? 뇌옥에 갇히는 게 버킷 리스트야?”
128|
129|“버귀…… 발음하기도 힘들군. 나로서는 그게 뭔지 잘 모르겠지만, 이미 감수하고 벌인 짓이다.”
130|
131|야율목이 나직한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
132|
133|“비록 부족은 다르지만 오랜 세월 같은 땅에서 함께한 남만인이다. 만약 동족을 죽인다면, 우리도 괴물이 되어 버리는 거야.”
134|
135|야율목의 말을 듣고 있자니 문득 한 사람이 떠올랐다. 오직 복수를 위한 괴물이 되어 버린 그가.
136|
137|‘백상.’
138|
139|그래, 어쩌면 이것이 인간과 괴물의 차이일지도 모르겠다.
140|
141|자신의 목적을 이루기 위해 덧없는 목숨을 희생시키지 않는 것. 그러나 나는 무거운 마음으로 입을 열었다.
142|
143|“모두 죽였어야 했어.”
144|
145|“살인을 좋아하는군. 한족들은 다 너처럼 그 모양인가?”
146|
147|“미친놈. 내가 마두(魔頭)라도 되는 줄 아냐? 이건 그냥…….”
148|
149|“그만하면 됐다. 말 안 해도 이미 알고 있으니까.”
150|
151|“뭐?”
152|
153|고개를 돌려보니, 야율목이 소리 없이 웃고 있었다.
154|
155|“우리가 걱정돼서 그런 거겠지. 널 구하려다가 곤경에 처했다는 죄책감 때문에.”
156|
157|“…….”
158|
159|“비록 중원과 언어는 다르지만, 벗이라는 단어는 남만에도 있다. 어쩌면 너와 내가 어느덧 그런 사이가 되었을지도 모르겠군. 아니면 나 혼자만의 착각이든지.”
160|
161|“……!”
162|
163|빌어먹을. 도무지 무슨 말을 해야 할지 모르겠다.
164|
165|내가 할 말을 잃은 그때, 끝없이 위로 이어져 있던 계단이 끝나고 마침내 뇌옥의 입구가 모습을 드러냈다.
166|
167|“원후.”
168|
169|야율목의 부름에 고개를 끄덕인 중년인이 앞으로 나선다.
170|
171|원숭이를 닮은 그가 커다란 열쇠 꾸러미를 차례대로 꽂자, 묵직한 소음과 함께 거대한 철문이 열리기 시작했다.
172|
173|구구구궁.
174|
175|서서히 열리는 철문 너머로 은은한 달빛이 새어 들어온 그때, 야율목이 품에서 자그마한 목갑 두 개를 꺼냈다.
176|
177|“공력의 금제를 풀 수 있는 해약(解藥)이다. 백족의 비전으로 만들어진 물건이라 두 개밖에 구하지 못했지만, 공력을 회복한 너라면 능히 다른 이들을 이끌고 남만을 빠져나갈 수 있을 것이다.”
178|
179|“다른 이들이라면 혹시?”
180|
181|“노인과 부상자라 그래서인지는 몰라도 경계가 매우 취약하더군. 적어도 그 부분에 있어서만큼은 철두철미한 백 숙부답지 못했어.”
182|
183|야율목의 대답과 동시에 나는 볼 수 있었다. 완전히 열린 철문 너머로 의식을 잃은 채 백호의 등에 실려 있는 두 사람을.
184|
185|“주군! 남호!”
186|
187|반가운 얼굴들을 발견한 태산은 헐레벌떡 뇌옥을 빠져나갔고, 나는 복잡한 표정으로 야율목을 응시했다.
188|
189|“너…….”
190|
191|“가라. 우리가 가급적 최대한 시간을 끌어 줄 테니. 물론 길어야 반 시진 안에 발각되겠지만 약간의 도움은 될 거다.”
192|
193|모르겠다. 이 상황에서 무슨 말을 해야 할지.
194|
195|만약 이들의 도움이 없었다면 어떻게 되었을까.
196|
197|나와 태산, 단둘이서 자력으로 뇌옥을 탈출할 수는 있었어도 결코 지금처럼 신속하게 남만야수궁을 빠져나올 수는 없었을 것이다.
198|
199|내게 있어 내궁 어딘가에 억류되어 있던 남호와 사마표의 존재는, 만근의 철구 이상으로 강력한 구속이었으니까.
200|
201|‘어쩌면 그 과정에서 다시 사로잡혔을지도 모르지.’
202|
203|하지만 이들은 혼신의 힘을 다해 나를 도왔다. 자신들이 위험에 처할 것을 감수하면서까지.
204|
205|그 덕분에 나는 악수(惡手)를 무를 수 있는 두 번째 기회를 얻을 수 있게 되었다.
206|
207|“……고맙다.”
208|
209|지금까지 미처 하지 못했던 감사 인사에, 야율목과 칠묘호. 그리고 뇌옥 밖에서 백족 전사들로 위장하고 있던 이들까지 희미한 미소를 지으며 고개를 저었다.
210|
211|“고마워할 필요 없소.”
212|
213|“그럼. 그저 남만이 당신에게 진 빚을 갚은 것뿐이지.”
214|
215|“애뇌산에 제 형이 있었습니다. 은공 덕분에 다시 만날 수 있게 되었지요.”
216|
217|얼굴도, 이름도 모르는 이들이 나를 도왔고 누군가는 은공이라 부른다.
218|
219|나는 그 모두의 얼굴을 한 사람, 한 사람 눈에 담았다.
220|
221|그리고 야율목의 손에 들린 목갑을 받아들고 흐릿한 달빛 아래로 걸음을 내디뎠다.
222|
223|사박.
224|
225|축축하게 젖어 있는 땅을 밟은 그 순간.
226|
227|띠링.
228|
229|
230|
231|- 처형 집행 전까지 뇌옥 탈출(완료)
232|
233|- 퀘스트 성공 조건을 달성하셨습니다!
234|
235|- 퀘스트, [남생크 탈출]을 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
236|
237|- 퀘스트 완료 보상을 지급합니다!
238|
239|- 막대한 경험치를 획득했습니다!
240|
241|- 레벨 업!
242|
243|- 일부 부상과 상태 이상이 해제됩니다!
244|
245|
246|
247|귓가를 파고드는 퀘스트 알림과 함께, 오직 나만이 느낄 수 있는 시원한 바람이 전신을 휩쓸었다.
248|
249|솨아아아!
250|
251|꼬박 하루가 넘는 시간 동안 뻣뻣하게 굳어 있던 근육. 아직 턱없이 부족한 중단전의 힘을 억지로 끌어올리느라 피로가 누적된 전신이 회복되고, 마지막으로 하단전(下丹田)을 옭아매고 있던 힘이 힘없이 녹아내린다.
252|
253|후우.
254|
255|크게 내뱉은 날숨에 열양지기로부터 흘러나온 열기가 뒤섞였다.
256|
257|그런 내 모습에 무언가를 느낀 듯, 야율목과 칠묘호가 눈을 크게 떴다.
258|
259|‘놀랍기도 하겠지. 아직 해약은 복용하지도 않았으니까.’
260|
261|하지만 미주알고주알 설명해 줄 생각도, 시간도 없는 상황이다.
262|
263|태산에게 간식이라며 목갑 안의 단환을 던져 준 나는, 정신을 잃은 사마표에게도 나머지 하나를 먹였다.
264|
265|화륵, 스르륵.
266|
267|열양지기에 의해 물처럼 녹아내리는 단환. 액체로 화한 단환이 그대로 목을 넘어가자, 약간 창백했던 사마표의 얼굴에 혈색이 돈다.
268|
269|‘생각보다 상태가 괜찮긴 하지만…… 당분간은 무리하면 안 돼.’
270|

Soft crunch.

[P105]
My foot touched the damp ground.

[P106]
Ding!

[P107]
> **System**
>
> - Escape from the underground prison before the execution (**Complete**)
> - You have fulfilled the Quest success conditions!
> - You have successfully completed the Quest, **Escape from Namshank**!
> - Issuing the Quest completion Reward!
> - You obtained a massive amount of EXP!
> - Level Up!
> - Some injuries and Status Effects have been removed!

[P108]
As the Quest notifications rang in my ears, a cool breeze that only I could feel swept through my body.

[P109]
Whoooosh!

[P110]
My muscles, stiff for more than a full day, loosened. The fatigue that had built up as I forced out the still woefully insufficient power of the Middle Dantian faded. Finally, the force constricting my Lower Dantian melted away.

[P111]
Hoo.

[P112]
Heat from the Scorching Yang Qi mingled with my long exhale.

[P113]
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers stared at me, eyes wide. They must have sensed something.

[P114]
*No wonder they’re surprised. I haven’t even taken the antidote.*

[P115]
But I had neither the time nor the intention to explain every little detail.

[P116]
I tossed Taishan a pill from one of the wooden cases, telling him it was a snack, then fed the other to the unconscious Sama Pyo.

[P117]
Fwoosh. Sssslip.

[P118]
The Scorching Yang Qi melted the pill like water. As the liquid ran down Sama Pyo’s throat, color returned to his slightly pale face.

[P119]
*He’s in better shape than I expected, but he shouldn’t push himself for a while.*

[P120]
Namho aside, losing Sama Pyo’s full strength as a fighter was a serious disadvantage. But it didn’t mean we couldn’t escape.

[P121]
If anything, we were in a better position than before I’d surrendered.

[P122]
*We’ve got everyone except the reconnaissance squad, and I’ve gained a little insight too.*

[P123]
Then Yayul Mok offered one more kindness I hadn’t expected.

[P124]

[P125]
Grrrr.

[P126]
A familiar growl.

[P127]

[P128]
“Muyaho is called a spiritual creature even among Nanman’s White Tigers. He’s like a brother to me. I trust you’ll take good care of him.”

[P129]

[P130]
Yayul Mok gave him a faint smile and pointed in one direction.

[P131]
“Go. Run straight northeast from where we first met, and you’ll find the reconnaissance squad.”

[P132]
That was when it happened.

[P133]
Thud.

[P134]

[P135]
“I trust you understand without my having to say it.”

[P136]
“You people…”

[P137]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Breaking my restraints had already consumed an enormous amount of mental strength. After one brief fight on top of that, my stomach was churning and my chest had begun to hurt. Taishan’s arrival was like getting an entire army as reinforcements.

[P9]
“Gwoooooooh!”

[P10]
Hmm. Actually, he was closer to the Hulk.

[P11]
And it wasn’t just the presence of a Supreme Peak master that made the enemy surrender so quickly. Taishan’s eerie muttering had a lot to do with it.

[P12]
“%#$%&^&%^&%^#$!”

[P13]
“Gasp!”

[P14]
His eyes gleamed with hunger.

[P15]
To the Bai warriors, the sight of Taishan approaching while spitting out incomprehensible words at machine-gun speed must have been terrifying. But I knew exactly what his incantation meant.

[P16]
“Roast duck! Maechae Guyuk[^1]! Fish-Fragrant Shredded Pork! Beijing Sauce Shredded Pork! Garlic Pork! Twice-Cooked Pork! Sweet and Sour Pork! Soy-Braised Beef! Dongpo Pork! Mapo Tofu!”

[P17]
“……”

[P18]
“Kung Pao Chicken! Stir-Fried Mushrooms and Vegetables! King-Size Dumplings! Beggar’s Chicken! Sweet-and-Sour Carp! Aaaaaaah!”

[P19]
Hmm.

[P20]
Good thing they couldn’t understand Han Chinese. Then again, a man slowly approaching while chanting food names like he was possessed might have been even scarier.

[P21]
“Hungryyyyyyyyy!”

[P22]
“Eek! Dark arts! That monster’s about to use dark arts!”

[P23]
“I surrender! I surrender!”

[P24]
That bastard was a Saiyan, at least by Nanman standards.

[P25]
Judging by their reactions, you’d think he’d shouted “Kamehameha!” instead of “I’m hungry!”

[P26]
Whatever I thought of it, his cry of hunger worked. Even the few brave men who stepped forward despite it got smashed by Taishan, and that settled the matter.

[P27]
“Don’t be afraid! Charge!”

[P28]
“We can do this! Strike him!”

[P29]
The men who came forward were skilled enough to be considered decent Supreme First Rate masters even in the Central Plains.

[P30]
Their only problem was who they’d chosen to fight.

[P31]
Thud! Craaack!

[P32]
Crack-crack!

[P33]
Taishan swung his log-thick arms and legs, sending bodies flying in every direction.

[P34]
The Bai warriors swallowed hard and lowered their weapons. Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers stared at me in disbelief.

[P35]
“What? What are you looking at?”

[P36]
“No, it’s just… wasn’t your internal energy sealed?”

[P37]
“Yeah. It was. I still can’t use it.”

[P38]
“……Then how?”

[P39]
“Mine’s a long story. That guy was born like that.”

[P40]
The human body had limits. I’d surpassed them by an absurd margin thanks to the System, but Taishan was a naturally occurring monster. Even without internal energy, he could beat down a First Rate master as easily as a rat.

[P41]
*Was he exposed to gamma radiation as a kid or something?*

[P42]
A reasonable suspicion, but it didn’t matter right now.

[P43]
I looked at the Bai warriors who had lost their will to fight and laid down their weapons.

[P44]
“All right. Let’s deal with this lot first.”

[P45]
* * *

[P46]
The short version is that the Bai warriors who surrendered survived. More precisely, Yayul Mok spared them.

[P47]
Thud. Slump.

[P48]
A warrior struck by a Pressure-Point Strike lost consciousness and fell. The Seven Miao Tigers, whom I’d gotten to know a few days earlier on the way to Ailao Mountain, gathered the unconscious warriors in one place and locked them in the underground prison. Then we headed straight for the stairs to the surface.

[P49]
Squelch.

[P50]
“I told you before… you’re going to regret this.”

[P51]
I said it as we walked. Yayul Mok understood what I meant and shook his head.

[P52]
“No, I won’t.”

[P53]
“Our faces are out in the open. Once they wake up, whose name do you think they’ll give first?”

[P54]
Yayul Mok was the Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace. That alone said enough. The Seven Miao Tigers were also well-known warriors who represented the Miao people. Their tribes might be different, but some of the prisoners had probably recognized them already.

[P55]
“It’s only a matter of time before this comes out. We should’ve silenced them.”

[P56]
“It doesn’t matter.”

[P57]
“Like hell it doesn’t. You’re not leaving with us, so how could it not matter? If you stay here…”

[P58]
“Our identities will be revealed. Our lives won’t be in immediate danger, but we’ll pay dearly for defying the Tribal Grand Council’s decision.”

[P59]
“I hate to ask, but do you enjoy getting fucked over? Is being locked in the underground prison on your bucket list?”

[P60]
“Bucki… I can hardly pronounce it. I don’t know what that is, but I knew the risk when I did this.”

[P61]
Yayul Mok continued quietly.

[P62]
“Our tribes are different, but we’re all Nanman people. We’ve lived together on this land for a long time. If we kill our own people, we become monsters too.”

[P63]
His words brought someone to mind. A man who had become a monster for the sake of revenge.

[P64]
*Baeksang.*

[P65]
Maybe that was the difference between a human being and a monster: refusing to sacrifice lives for your own ends.

[P66]
Even so, I spoke with a heavy heart.

[P67]
“We should’ve killed them all.”

[P68]
“You do like killing. Are all Han Chinese like you?”

[P69]
“You crazy bastard. Do you think I’m some kind of fiend? It’s just…”

[P70]
“That’s enough. I already know.”

[P71]
“What?”

[P72]
I turned to find Yayul Mok smiling silently.

[P73]
“You’re worried about us. You feel guilty because we got ourselves into trouble trying to save you.”

[P74]
“……”

[P75]
“The Central Plains and Nanman have different languages, but we have a word for *friend* too. Perhaps that’s what you and I have become without realizing it. Unless I’m the only one who thinks so.”

[P76]
“……!”

[P77]
Damn it. I had no idea what to say.

[P78]
While I stood there speechless, the seemingly endless stairs finally came to an end. The entrance to the underground prison was before us.

[P79]
“Wonhu.”

[P80]
At Yayul Mok’s call, the middle-aged man nodded and stepped forward. He looked like a monkey. He tried the keys on a large ring one after another, and the enormous iron door began to open with a heavy rumble.

[P81]
Grooooan.

[P82]
Faint moonlight slipped through the widening gap. Yayul Mok took two small wooden cases from inside his robes.

[P83]
“An antidote to lift the seal on your internal energy. It’s made with a secret Bai technique, so I could only get two. Once your internal energy is restored, you should be able to lead the others out of Nanman.”

[P84]
“The others?”

[P85]
“I don’t know if it was because they’re old and injured, but security around them was remarkably lax. Uncle Baeksang isn’t usually so careless.”

[P86]
As Yayul Mok spoke, I saw them beyond the fully opened door: two unconscious people lying across a White Tiger’s back.

[P87]
“Lord! Namho!”

[P88]
Taishan rushed out of the prison toward the familiar faces. I stared at Yayul Mok, my feelings tangled.

[P89]
“You…”

[P90]
“Go. We’ll buy you as much time as we can. They’ll discover what happened within half a shichen at most, but even that should help.”

[P91]
I didn’t know what to say.

[P92]
What would have happened without their help?

[P93]
Taishan and I might have escaped the underground prison on our own, but we could never have gotten out of the Nanman Beast Palace this quickly. As long as Namho and Sama Pyo were being held somewhere in the Inner Palace, I was bound more tightly than I’d been by ten thousand geun of iron balls.

[P94]
*I might’ve been captured again trying to get them out.*

[P95]
But these people had given everything they had to help me, knowing the danger it put them in.

[P96]
Thanks to them, I had a second chance to undo my bad move.

[P97]
“……Thank you.”

[P98]
At the thanks I hadn’t managed to give them before, Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers smiled faintly and shook their heads. So did the people outside the prison who had disguised themselves as Bai warriors.

[P99]
“No need to thank us.”

[P100]
“That’s right. We’re only repaying a debt Nanman owes you.”

[P101]
“My hyung was on Ailao Mountain. Thanks to you, I’ll get to see him again.”

[P102]
People whose faces and names I didn’t know had helped me. One even called me his benefactor.

[P103]
I looked at each of them, committing their faces to memory. Then I took the wooden cases from Yayul Mok and stepped into the faint moonlight.

[P104]
Soft crunch.

[P105]
My foot touched the damp ground.

[P106]
Ding!

[P107]
> **System**
>
> - Escape from the underground prison before the execution (**Complete**)
> - You have fulfilled the Quest success conditions!
> - You have successfully completed the Quest, **Escape from Namshank**!
> - Issuing the Quest completion Reward!
> - You obtained a massive amount of EXP!
> - Level Up!
> - Some injuries and Status Effects have been removed!

[P108]
As the Quest notifications rang in my ears, a cool breeze that only I could feel swept through my body.

[P109]
Whoooosh!

[P110]
My muscles, stiff for more than a full day, loosened. The fatigue that had built up as I forced out the still woefully insufficient power of the Middle Dantian faded. Finally, the force constricting my Lower Dantian melted away.

[P111]
Hoo.

[P112]
Heat from the Scorching Yang Qi mingled with my long exhale.

[P113]
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers stared at me, eyes wide. They must have sensed something.

[P114]
*No wonder they’re surprised. I haven’t even taken the antidote.*

[P115]
But I had neither the time nor the intention to explain every little detail.

[P116]
I tossed Taishan a pill from one of the wooden cases, telling him it was a snack, then fed the other to the unconscious Sama Pyo.

[P117]
Fwoosh. Sssslip.

[P118]
The Scorching Yang Qi melted the pill like water. As the liquid ran down Sama Pyo’s throat, color returned to his slightly pale face.

[P119]
*He’s in better shape than I expected, but he shouldn’t push himself for a while.*

[P120]
Namho aside, losing Sama Pyo’s full strength as a fighter was a serious disadvantage. But it didn’t mean we couldn’t escape.

[P121]
If anything, we were in a better position than before I’d surrendered.

[P122]
*We’ve got everyone except the reconnaissance squad, and I’ve gained a little insight too.*

[P123]
Then Yayul Mok offered one more kindness I hadn’t expected.

[P124]
“Take him with you.”

[P125]
Grrrr.

[P126]
A familiar growl.

[P127]
The White Tiger looked sadly at the friend and master who had been with him all his life, then offered me his back.

[P128]
“Muyaho is called a spiritual creature even among Nanman’s White Tigers. He’s like a brother to me. I trust you’ll take good care of him.”

[P129]
As though he understood Yayul Mok’s subdued voice, the White Tiger licked my hand, then pressed his nose against me and sniffed.

[P130]
Yayul Mok gave him a faint smile and pointed in one direction.

[P131]
“Go. Run straight northeast from where we first met, and you’ll find the reconnaissance squad.”

[P132]
That was when it happened.

[P133]
Thud.

[P134]
At the sound of a blow, Yayul Mok’s body jerked. Wonhu caught him as he collapsed, then grinned at me.

[P135]
“I trust you understand without my having to say it.”

[P136]
“You people…”

[P137]
“Please look after the Young Palace Lord.”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
